research_rationale:
EO 12648 (53 FR 30637, signed 1988-08-11, published 1988-08-15) is a one-section order. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12648.txt, page 7 of the August 15, 1988 issue; its heading names Executive Order 12648 of August 11, 1988, 'Relating to the Implementation of the Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction'). The preamble recites that the Convention entered into force for the United States on July 1, 1988 and that the order is issued under section 7 of the International Child Abduction Remedies Act; section 1 designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform the acts needed to execute the Central Authority's functions. The held text has no sunset, condition, deadline or termination language. The current predicate uses the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches, because the U.S. Code release-point zip (sha256 c6122974e951003437ece5a998aa7c0b2cdc0f5703dfc78d6135e1fc9e729142) is held only as a custody record; the Code note printing the order under 22 U.S.C. 9006 note is therefore a lead I read but do not cite as a source. Coverage notes read: current-law:usc covers the U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected); current-law:ecfr is an eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 plus GovInfo CFR bulk XML; later-events:ofr_catalog covers disposition notes of 6,941 OFR catalog records and operative sentences in 17,746 saved order texts. The three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) found no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes the order, so no later event is attached. The held texts that cite the number are the order's own Federal Register text and the 1989 codification snapshot only. This is a claim on the held official Federal Register text; the 2026 predicate rests on the Code note and the bounded searches, not on a consolidated agency source.
